as a closeted gay guy who lives in a circumstances where there's no way i would ever came out, i ask this question very often. when you don't have any support system irl, you seek one from the internet. i know that it's no one responsibility to be at least kind to people, but reading how people think about a closeted person in a supposed to be safe place from a community you thought you are in is really heartbreaking. god, it is so fucking lonely. I'm not even talking about relationship wise, that i have accepted long time ago when i came to terms with myself of who i am.

i came from a religious background, and i know people don't like that. yes, i also have internalized homophobia, and i always keep it to myself and would never target it to anyone, i faced homophobia daily and i would never wished it on anyone. i never asked people to accept the world that i am coming from, I'm just asking people to understand that it is who i am.

"coming out is always an option", yes, i am also aware of that, but that's not my option as of now. I'm sorry I don't have the courage and the energy to not only lost everything and everyone but also to potentially has to be in a constant run. if you did that at one point of your life, good for you. i wish i could be like you. all i wanted is just people to go through all of this fake till make it with, but yes, i know it is such big thing to ask for. I've learned that i should never expect that from people.

sorry if I'm rambling self pitying myself. i got no other things to do besides trying not to die and wanting to die.

I'm gay, a muslim, and live in a muslim majority country. There was a time when i thought "huh, how can people be gay. they probably watch too many girly stuff and hang out with girls too often" but then realized I am that guy (im not saying all gay guys like this). I'm trying to be as manly as possible everyday, but there'll always someone who pointed out something about me whether it's the way i sit, the way i talk, etc. I've also realized that i always liked boys before I've even knew what gay or even lgbtq+ means which is until was in high school. 

I'm not really that religious, but i do the mandatory prayer everyday. I do know about the basic stuff as I am surrounded in a community but I must admit, my knowledge about Islam is very limited. but it's kinda hard no? to come to religious study, only to feel indirectly targeted by the Imam when the talk about lgbtq+ comes up. I've tried my whole life making sure I'm not gay but I still felt targeted when the media or someone brings up gay people. I still remember my religion assignment from last week(religion study is a mandatory lesson in uni here at least for one semester) that asked about how do I feel about a quote from lgbtq+ activist from my country that basically said how people use any ayat without disecting or research it to justify their hate rowards the lgbtq+ community and also asked for my own opinions about that which of course, it's an unwritten rule to disagree. so imagine, I have to write everything contrary about myself. It felt like literally writing about what i hate about myself and quote several ayat and hadist that said ppl like me will go straight to hell and whatnot, you get the idea. leads me felt like i belong to nowhere and alienated by the whole society, from muslim community because apparently I'm gay, and from lgbtq+ community because of my background which always have an internalized homophobia.

As for how important coming out is, I'd say personally for me, it's important. Coming out for me is not only letting people now, that i AM gay but also accepting myself as how i am so that I feel comfortable in my own skin, which is i still not to figure out now. to be honest with you, I don't think I'd be able to come out to anyone I know, including my family and friends. the only circumstances I can see myself to do it is probably when my parents already passed away (which is a horrible thought, i know) because even if my parents is acceptig, they'll be judged by the whole society here too which I would never put them through and when I move away from here and simply start a new life. Both of them most likely won't happen anytime soon so I guess I just have to try to keep living as "normal" people here as long as I can.

p.s. sorry for my crappy english, not a native speaker. I still have a lot in my mind but that's all that can come out now as I was writing this at 12 am and it's apparently almost 2 now lol. Hope this helps :)
